text.p: Italy said on Wednesday it aimed to organise talks "as soon as possible" between world bodies, European experts and Albanian authorities to agree economic measures to help the troubled Balkan country.

Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told a parliamentary joint commission that emergency humanitarian aid to Albania must be accompanied by a "global initiative to rehabilitate the country's economic and financial system."
"In that area, Italy intends to call as soon as possible a "Stabilisation Conference"," he said.

Dini said international financial bodies, the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, European Commission experts and the Albanian authorities would be invited to "agree the main lines of intervention and appropriate measures to apply."
He did not say where the meeting would take place.
About 300 people have been killed and 700 injured in weeks of anarchy that swept Europe's poorest nation after pyramid investment schemes wiped out the savings of thousands of Albanian families.
Albanian finance minister Arben Malaj said on Tuesday that the "pyramid" savings schemes were worth about half the impoverished country's national income.
He called then for a meeting with donors and international investors as soon as possible in a bid to kick-start an economy throttled by months of anarchy.

"We have it confirmed from Italy that it will invite donors, possible donors and others to an international conference," Malaj said at the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in London.
Relief agencies have estimated that one in 10 Albanians needs humanitarian aid.
Italy is leading an eight-nation mission, dubbed Operation Alba (Dawn) which will eventually number 6,000 soldiers, to protect aid deliveries to Albania.
The first troops began arriving on Tuesday.
